title: `@object-ui/fields` deep subpaths resolve only through the repo vitest alias — its `exports` map publishes none of them
body:
Observation-class finding, surfaced while wiring `@object-ui/plugin-detail`'s tests into `tsc` for #4040 (tranche 3). Nothing a user meets today — the one live consumer is a test, and it passes.

## What

`packages/fields/package.json` publishes exactly two entry points:

```json
"exports": {
  ".":           { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/index.js", "require": "./dist/index.cjs" },
  "./style.css": "./dist/index.css"
}
```

`packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/RelatedList.longFormColumns.test.tsx:45` imports a third:

```
import '@object-ui/fields/widgets/MarkdownContent';
```

That specifier resolves because `vitest.config.mts:251` aliases the whole package name to its SOURCE directory (`'@object-ui/fields': packages/fields/src`), so the deep path lands on `packages/fields/src/widgets/MarkdownContent.tsx`. Nothing else makes it resolvable: it is not in the `exports` map, and `dist` has no matching layout. Under Node's own resolution — or any consumer outside this repo's vitest config — it is a bare `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`.

It is the only deep `@object-ui/fields/...` import in the repo (`grep -rn "@object-ui/fields/widgets" packages --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` returns that one line), so the blast radius today is one test file.

## How it surfaced

Type-checking plugin-detail's tests puts the file in front of `tsc` with `paths: {}` — the template every wired-up package uses, so that workspace deps resolve through their built `.d.ts` rather than pulling sibling sources in. The compiler then asks the same question Node would and gets the same answer:

```
src/__tests__/RelatedList.longFormColumns.test.tsx(34,8): error TS2882: Cannot find module or type
  declarations for side-effect import of '@object-ui/fields/widgets/MarkdownContent'.
```

The import is not removable — it is load-bearing. The two "no column derived" cases assert `queryByText('Heading')` **synchronously** after awaiting only the row, and `MarkdownContent` sits behind `React.lazy` in `packages/fields/src/index.tsx:1711`. Without the module-scope pre-load, a wrongly-derived richtext column would still read as absent while its chunk was in flight, i.e. green for the wrong reason. So PR (this tranche) keeps the import and restates the alias as a narrow `paths` entry in `packages/plugin-detail/tsconfig.test.json`, scoped to `widgets/*` so no other sibling source can leak in behind it.

That entry is a workaround for this gap and is commented as one. It is also the reason this is worth recording: the test tsconfig now carries a source-tree path that every other wired-up package avoided on purpose.

## Worth knowing: the comment that came off with it

The line's original comment claimed the specifier was "Same specifier the component uses". It is not — the component uses a package-relative `import('./widgets/MarkdownContent')` from inside `fields`' own index. The two happen to resolve to the same module id under the alias, which is why the pre-load works at all, but the stated reason was wrong. Corrected in the same PR.

## Why it is `finding` and not queued

No user-visible behaviour depends on it, and the fix is one of two shapes — a product call about the package's surface, not a code one:

- **The subpath is intended** — long-form cell widgets are a reasonable thing to import directly. Then `fields` should publish `./widgets/*` in its `exports` map (with the matching `dist` layout), and the `paths` entry in plugin-detail's test config goes away.
- **The subpath is not intended** — the package's surface is its index, and the test should pre-load through a sanctioned path instead. Then the alias making it work is the accident, and the test needs a different mechanism for the same anti-race guarantee.

Either way it wants a ruling on what `@object-ui/fields` publishes, rather than a guess made inside a test-infrastructure PR.

Refs #4040, objectstack-ai/objectstack#4118.
